title: Teacher expectancy and pupil IQ: 19 studies, standardized mean differences (Raudenbush 1984), dat.raudenbush1985
data_source: Raudenbush SW (2009). Analyzing effect sizes: random-effects models. In: Cooper H, Hedges LV, Valentine JC (eds), The Handbook of Research Synthesis and Meta-Analysis, 2nd ed., Russell Sage Foundation, pp. 295-315; Table 16.1 (p. 300). yi (standardized mean difference) and vi as listed at https://www.metafor-project.org/doku.php/analyses:raudenbush2009 (study 10 is 0.80, not the chapter's typo 0.87, cf. Raudenbush and Bryk 1985, Table 1).
notes: The effects are given as yi/vi, so this dataset validates SMD pooling (FE, DL, REML; Wald and Knapp-Hartung intervals), not the per-study SMD computation. The chapter's Table 16.3 prints 3 decimals; the 4-decimal references are metafor's rounded outputs that metafor's test suite (tests/testthat/test_analysis_example_raudenbush2009.r, CRAN metafor) checks against Table 16.3. I^2 values are metafor's printed rma() output on the metafor page. i2 is a proportion.

analyses.source: Raudenbush (2009), Table 16.2 (p. 301), p. 302 and Table 16.3 (p. 309), conventional fixed-effects row: metafor's 4-decimal outputs as checked in metafor's test_analysis_example_raudenbush2009.r; I^2 from the rma(method="EE") output printed at metafor-project.org analyses:raudenbush2009

Raudenbush (2009), Table 16.3 (p. 309), conventional approach, REML row: metafor's 4-decimal outputs as checked in metafor's test_analysis_example_raudenbush2009.r; the prediction interval is metafor's predict(res.RE) as recorded in the same test file (the chapter's p. 302 interval, -0.19 to 0.35, is computed differently: mu +/- 1.96 tau); I^2 and Q from the rma() REML output printed at metafor-project.org analyses:raudenbush2009

expected.tolerance_note: metafor's REML tau^2 here is about 0.01883, slightly short of the fully converged 0.018818 (consistent with metafor stopping once tau^2 changes by < 1e-5); at tau^2 = 0.018829 this interval gives 0.3711

metafor's REML tau^2 here is about 0.01883, slightly short of the fully converged 0.018818 (consistent with metafor stopping once tau^2 changes by < 1e-5); I^2 = 41.86% corresponds to tau^2 = 0.018829, and dI^2/dtau^2 = 12.9 here

analyses.source: Raudenbush (2009), Table 16.3 (p. 309), conventional approach, method-of-moments row (= DerSimonian-Laird): metafor's 4-decimal outputs as checked in metafor's test_analysis_example_raudenbush2009.r; I^2 from the rma(method="DL") output printed at metafor-project.org analyses:raudenbush2009

Raudenbush (2009), Table 16.3 (p. 309), quasi-F (Knapp-Hartung) approach, REML row: metafor's 4-decimal outputs of rma(method="REML", test="knha") as checked in metafor's test_analysis_example_raudenbush2009.r (hksj="auto" resolves to HKSJ: tau^2 > 0, k = 19)
